Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you making time, I'm Ethan Ross from Redwood, Account Exec. With me is Priya, our Solutions Eng.
[00:12] Priya: Hi all, Priya Desai, I'll run through the console and the cost analytics sections. Quick note, audio looks good on my end.
[00:20] Marta: Hi, Marta here, Director of ML at Skyline. We've got Ken and Liam on as well. We're mainly looking at how to get predictable costs for a POC and also how the per-route dashboards will help with allocation.
[00:34] Liam: Yeah and we want to see the delta between hosted and dedicated for our transactional flows.
[00:42] Priya: Great. So agenda: quick product context, demo the Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, then cost breakdowns and routing policies, and Q&A. We'll leave time at the end for security questions.
[00:58] [screen share starts] Priya: Alright, opening the Redwood Console here — landing page, multi-tenant view, you can see top-level token usage, latency percentiles, and cost estimate. One small note, sometimes the auto-caption splits "KV cache" into "K V cash" in captions, so apologies if the transcript looks funny.
[01:20] Priya: Jumping into Usage Analytics: you can slice by time, model, route, and customer tag. For example, here's a 30-day view, token breakdown by prompt vs completion, and per-route QPS.
[01:36] Ken: Can you show how we map our internal routes? We have "inference/search-prod" and "autocomplete-user" routes.
[01:44] Priya: Yep, routes map to API endpoints or SDK keys — you can tag them and set cost centers. Here's the per-route dashboard for "inference/search-prod" — you get histogram of latencies, p95/p99, token counts, and a per-model cost column.
[02:05] Priya: Note the cost model is configurable — you can plug in Dedicated pool unit costs or hosted per-token rates. We also show the "effective unit cost" after batching and KV cache hits.
[02:22] Marta: About that, how do you surface caching benefits? We rely heavily on prefix caching for search.
[02:29] Priya: In the console we surface "cache hit rate" and estimated token savings; you can filter to see which routes and prompts benefit most. We also provide suggestions in Redwood Optimize — e.g., increase prefix cache TTL for certain routes. Sometimes the suggestion engine shows as "Optima" in captions — that's the transcription again.
[02:48] Ethan: For Skyline's POC we usually recommend modeling two representative routes: high-throughput short prompts (autocomplete) and lower-QPS long context (search re-rank). That gives a clearer cost/latency trade-off.
[03:06] [03:06] Priya: Now cost breakdown: here's a per-route table that splits cost by model variant, token type, and infra bucket. You can export CSV, and also tag costs to internal cost centers.
[03:22] Marta: Can you show an example where dedicated capacity lowers unit cost?
[03:27] Priya: Sure — switching to a Dedicated pool we apply the reserved unit price; the console will show a projected monthly cost delta based on your observed usage pattern. See the "Cost Simulator" modal — we input your QPS and it computes token/unit economics, including burst buffer fees.
[03:46] Ken: Does the cost sim account for batching improvements? Our autocomplete flow has a lot of short calls.
[03:52] Priya: Yes, we estimate batching gains based on request size distribution; you can also simulate applying continuous-batching or adjusting batch windows. The simulator is conservative by default.
[04:06] Liam: Any chance to hook this into our own billing system? We need per-route chargebacks into our finance tool.
[04:13] Priya: You can export reports or use the Cost API — it emits per-route cost snapshots; many customers connect to Snowflake/Looker or push to internal billing. We can share the API spec after.
[04:28] [04:28] Priya: Quick note on routing policies — you can set policies based on latency SLO, model cost, or region. For instance, route low-latency calls to a local Dedicated pool, and fallback to Hosted in other regions.
[04:44] Marta: For compliance, we need data residency and KMS control. Does the Console show per-request data residency metadata?
[04:51] Priya: Yes, requests carry metadata tags and the audit log shows which region served the request. For private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM and can keep logs within the VPC. We'll attach the private deployment checklist and KMS notes.
[05:08] Ethan: We'll also include the SOC2 pack and ISO docs in the follow-up; Priya will send those.
[05:15] [05:15] Marta: That'd be great. Also, what about RBAC? We want to limit who can change routing policies.
[05:21] Priya: Console supports RBAC roles and SSO via SAML/OIDC — you can restrict role to "Cost Analyst" "Admin" etc. Changes to routing or model pinning create an immutable audit event.
[05:34] Ken: Earlier you mentioned KV cache management and prefix caching. For long context calls, how do we handle KV eviction?
[05:41] Priya: The runtime exposes eviction metrics; console shows cache size, eviction rate, and suggested cache size by workload. There's also an API to pre-populate cache for warm start.
[05:54] [05:54] Marta: For benchmarking, what's the recommended window? We expect traffic spikes during promotions and steady baseline otherwise.
[06:02] Priya: We usually run a 48–72 hour representative sample capturing peak window; for promo spikes we can run synthetic load to measure tail latency and cost at scale. We'll run a pilot on a Dedicated pool if you want guaranteed SLOs.
[06:22] Liam: For the pilot, what's the onboarding timeline? We need to coordinate infra and security.
[06:27] Ethan: Typical pilot is 2–4 weeks for engineering onboarding + 1–2 week benchmark. Private deployments take longer. We'll put together a timeline after we get your sample dataset.
[06:40] [06:40] Priya: Back to the console — here's the per-route alerting config: set thresholds on p95/p99, cost-per-minute burn, or unexpected model swaps. Alerts can integrate with PagerDuty or Slack.
[06:56] Ken: Do you have examples of cost regressions being detected?
[07:02] Priya: Yes, the Quality & Cost monitor flags when per-route effective unit cost rises 20% vs baseline and will identify candidate causes (model change, prompt drift, cache drop). It also ties to evals so you can check quality regressions.
[07:22] Marta: Speaking of model changes, we sometimes want to A/B test a newer quantized variant. How do rollouts look in console?
[07:29] Priya: Rollouts are built-in: canary percent, time-based, or traffic-based split. You can pin a route to a model version or set automatic fallbacks if latency degrades. Rollouts are auditable.
[07:44] [07:44] Ethan: Quick objection handling — customers worry that dedicated commitment is risky. We show projected unit economics and provide burst capacity + fallback to hosted to avoid outages.
[08:00] Marta: Ok that's helpful. Do you have a sample invoice layout for finance?
[08:06] Priya: Yep, billing exports include per-route chargebacks, reserved capacity amortization, and one-off fees. We'll attach a sample invoice layout.
[08:16] Ken: Any concerns around downstream vendor models like Bedrock? We sometimes use Bedrock for certain workloads.
[08:22] Priya: We integrate with multiple backends; console lets you compare model performance across providers. If you run with Redwood-managed open models we give more runtime optimizations.
[08:34] [08:34] Marta: Can you show the drilldown for a specific spike last week?
[08:39] Priya: Sure — filtering to 2026-12-05 10:00–12:00, you can see a sudden p99 jump tied to a batch of long-context rerank requests. The log links show request payload sizes and the model used, plus a recommendation to increase batch window or spin up additional Dedicated workers.
[08:59] Liam: How precise is the cost attribution when requests hit caching layers and sometimes get served locally?
[09:05] Priya: We attribute costs to the originating route and then apply adjustments for cache hits; console shows gross vs net token usage. There can be a small delta for cross-region egress but it's surfaced.
[09:18] [09:18] Marta: We want to limit PII in logs. Can the audit log redact request text?
[09:24] Priya: Yes, you can configure redaction rules or disable full-text logging; for Private deployments we can keep logs inside your VPC and integrate with your SIEM.
[09:36] Ethan: Ok, quick recap, we'll send SOC2 + KMS notes, Dedicated pricing, and sample invoice. Priya will share the Console recording and the benchmark template.
[09:48] [09:48] Marta: Great. One final question: do you support per-tenant quotas? We want to ensure a single customer doesn't blow the pool.
[09:56] Priya: Yes, per-tenant and per-route quotas, throttles, and soft-fail patterns. The Console shows quota usage and estimated time to reset.
[10:08] [10:08] Ken: Thanks all, this was useful. We'll sync internally and get you the sample dataset.
[10:12] Ethan: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with next steps.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-hearings (Optima/Optimize), truncated words from auto-caption, speaker labels sometimes short (Priya as "Speaker 2" in raw transcript).
